rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a security deposit of no more than 1.5 times one month's rent. Any later yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. A pet deposit counts toward the same cap. Prepaid rent held to secure future rent, including last month's rent, counts as part of the deposit. A landlord may require the 1.5-month deposit plus the first month's rent at the start of the lease. The deposit stays the tenant's property and must be held in trust, not commingled, and kept in an interest-bearing account at an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan. The landlord must return the deposit plus interest within 30 days after the tenancy ends, less deductions. Deductions are limited to damage beyond normal wear and tear and other money due under the lease, and must be itemized by registered or certified mail. If the landlord fails to return the deposit on time, or the tenant disputes the deductions, the tenant may sue for double the deposit.
rules.key_value: Max 1.5 months' rent; yearly increase max 10% of the current deposit; return with interest within 30 days of tenancy end; itemized deductions by registered or certified mail; double damages for wrongful withholding

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Landlords receiving deposits for fewer than 10 units must use an interest-bearing account at an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan. Landlords with 10 or more units may alternatively invest in an insured money market fund of a New Jersey-based investment company.
coverage.summary: Applies to landlords collecting security deposits from residential tenants. The passages state no unit-count, age or owner-occupancy exemptions.

rules.quoted_span: cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).
rules.review_note: Based on an official tenant guide that summarizes the statutes, not the statutory text. No effective date is stated. The passages do not mention the pet-deposit or interest-rate details beyond what is summarized.
rules.source_notes: Secondary summary in an official guide (D067). Case law cited there treats prepaid rent as part of the deposit (Brownstone Arms v. Asher; Reilly v. Weiss).
